identity.title: The Anatomy of an Unusual Edge-on Protoplanetary Disk. I. Dust Settling in a Cold Disk

analysis_steps.goal: Measure ALMA continuum flux and geometry

method.value: Aperture photometry in CASA with 3 sigma cut; imfit for comparison; profiles along major/minor axes

evidence.quote: we perform aperture photometry in the CASA software package with a 3$\sigma$ cut (with an rms of 0.134 mJy)
where we have assumed a conservative flux error of 10%

validation.value: Compared with imfit integrated flux of ~47 mJy

evidence.quote: this is consistent with the integrated flux value of $\sim 47$ mJy provided by the CASA imfit package

analysis_steps.goal: Individual MCMC fits to F814W and ALMA images

method.value: MCFOST models convolved with Tiny Tim PSF or ALMA Gaussian beam, normalised to observed flux, recentred, chi-square log-likelihood on pixels >3 sigma

evidence.quote: we first generate a synthetic image with MCFOST at the specified wavelength, convolve this model with an instrumental PSF, normalize the model to the sum of the observed disk signal
For both initial runs we use a parallel-tempered sampler with 2 temperatures and 50 walkers.

key_parameters.value: Free: i, H0, dust mass, gamma, beta, p, alpha, Rc; fixed distance 147 pc, Rin 1 au, Rout 191 au

evidence.quote: The disk is assumed to be at a distance of 147 pc with an inner radius fixed at 1 au and an outer radius of 191 au.

assumptions.value: Single species amorphous olivine, non-porous grains, a = 0.03-1000 micron, 70 log bins

evidence.quote: with a particle size distribution described by a power law extending from $a$ = 0.03 - 1000 $\mu$m in size

fitting.value: Uniform priors except uniform in cos i and log-uniform for dust mass and alpha; ranges in Table 2

evidence.quote: We use uniform priors for all parameters except for the inclination (uniform in $\cos{i}$), and the dust mass and viscosity parameter where log-uniform priors are used.

validation.value: Effective sample size from integrated autocorrelation time

evidence.quote: We compute an effective sample size (ESS) for each parameter to test the convergence of the chain.

method.value: Gaussian likelihood with covariance C = diag noise + global covariance from residual autocorrelation of 1000 models from individual runs; ALMA downsampled to HST resolution; p fixed at 3.5

evidence.quote: We generate an autocorrelation map by selecting 1000 models drawn from the MCMC chain, computing the observation - model residuals, and autocorrelating those residuals.

key_parameters.value: 2 temperatures, 50 walkers, 2000 iterations, burn-in 250; covariance cutoff at 8 pixels

evidence.quote: with a cutoff outside of 8 pixels to make computations of $C_{i,j}$ tractable

fitting.value: Same priors as individual fits with p fixed

evidence.quote: For the combined MCMC run we keep this value fixed at 3.5 to further limit parameter degeneracies.

validation.value: ESS test; only inclination and gamma unconstrained (ESS 8 and 20)

evidence.quote: only the inclination and surface density exponent remain unconstrained with ESS values of 8 and 20, respectively

analysis_steps.goal: Compare models with SED and Keck image; derive scale heights and Stokes numbers

method.value: Compare representative models A, B, C to SED and 2.2 micron profiles; compute temperature-derived scale height and Stokes numbers

evidence.quote: we compute the Stokes numbers for Models A, B and C following (cite: 2016SSRv..205...41B)
we assume a reduced mass, $\mu$ of 2.3

validation.value: Cross-check with CO-derived temperature in Paper II

evidence.quote: We find that the vertical extent of the gas matches the HST scattered light observations
The MCFOST radiative transfer code (cite: 2006A&A...459..797P; 2009A&A...498..967P) was used to construct synthetic SEDs
we employ a parallel-tempered Monte Carlo Markov Chain approach using the `emcee` package

findings_qualitative.value: Disk is flared but vertically thin; some dust settling is required to reconcile scattered light and mm datasets; midplane colder than expected.

evidence.quote: some degree of dust settling is required to reproduce the vertically thin profile and lack of apparent flaring

claims.hypothesis: Can a single smooth tapered disk model fit both scattered light and ALMA continuum?
claims.experiment: Separate chi-square and joint covariance MCMC runs with MCFOST
claims.result: Individual fits good; joint fit gives worse fit and bimodal dust mass posterior
claims.finding: Model lacks complexity; more complex radial structure likely

evidence.quote: It is apparent that the simple disk model we have employed here lacks sufficient complexity to explain both datasets simultaneously.

claims.experiment: Compare apparent vertical extent in scattered light and mm; alpha posterior
claims.result: Low alpha values ruled out; mm scale heights smaller than 0.8 micron

evidence.quote: some degree of settling is certainly required to explain the variation in the apparent dust scale height

why_this_method.value: Covariance likelihood to combine datasets with different noise and sensitivities without biasing the fit

evidence.quote: to leverage the information inherent in both datasets without preferentially biasing the fit towards one image or the other

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Keck image and other HST filters excluded from fitting

evidence.quote: We chose not to include the Keck image in the modeling because of the image artifacts

limitations_admitted.value: Midplane thermal emission not vertically resolved; smooth tapered density model too simple

evidence.quote: since the vertical height of the disk in the ALMA data is not resolved

referee_caveats_inferred: Model fits are degenerate; posteriors often hit prior edges
Fitting image-plane CLEAN map rather than visibilities
Joint fit has ESS of 8 for inclination
Flux normalisation marginalised so absolute mass poorly constrained
